messages:
eva: FYI — customer on Dedicated saw their burst cushion go to 0 and then not refill for ~7m after we removed a priority throttle. They hit 429s during a short rebuild job. Can we check the replenishment path?

morgan: Which customer / pool? any repro?

eva: tenant_id 5f8a9c, dedicated pool 'eu-west-3-gpud-1'. They ran a backfill that spiked token usage ~6x for 45s. After we lifted the emergency throttle we expected the burst credits to start refilling but they stayed at 0.

ira: Can you paste the API error sample from the customer's side? Also did the console show any quota transition events?

eva: Customer sent this snippet from their client: ```json
{"status":429, "error":"rate_limited", "detail":"burst_cushion_exhausted"}
```

morgan: Thanks. Looking at control-plane logs for that pool: I see a throttle applied at 2678912200 for 90s — a priority throttle because the node reported an OOM-ish slow degrade. When throttle removed at 2678912290 the reward/refill job ran but returned transient 503s to the pool manager.

ira: That 503 to refill job could explain delayed state update. Refill jobs are best-effort; if manager rejects, metric persists. Any kube events?

morgan: Found this on node gpud-3: `EvictionThreshold exceeded, memory_pressure=true`, then kubelet restarted some containers. There are logs where the refill RPC timed out with `context deadline exceeded`.

alex-p: Two quick asks for repro: 1) a short script that simulates their backfill pattern so we can replay on staging; 2) a small timeline of their client retries (so we know if client hammered after 429s).

eva: I asked customer for the retry timeline. For repro I spun up a local sim using the SDK:```bash
# simulate 45s spike, 6x baseline
for i in $(seq 1 900); do 
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"input":"x"}' &
  sleep 0.05
done
```
This reproduces transient 429s when run against a small dedicated pool in my dev env.

ira: Good. Add these checks: 
- confirm refill RPC success logs (control-plane -> pool-manager)
- confirm burst_credit state transition events (state: exhausted -> replenishing -> available)
- check whether priority throttle sets a cooldown that prevents immediate refill for X seconds (bug candidate)

morgan: I see a cooldown flag in the code path: when priority throttle applied for safety we set a refill_delay = max( refill_delay, throttle_duration / 2 ). Intended to prevent oscillation. But in this case because the refill RPC hit transient 503s the refill state machine didn't advance and cooldown kept blocking.

eva: So sequence was: spike -> safety throttle -> refill job attempted but RPC failures -> cooldown still counts -> customer kept retrying -> 429s continued.

alex-p: Proposed next steps:
1) short-term: manually trigger a forced refill for that pool (control-plane admin endpoint) so the customer recovers now.
2) medium-term: add retry/backoff to refill RPC (3 attempts, exponential backoff) and emit an alert if refill fails 2x in a row.
3) long-term: make the cooldown policy bounded (cap at e.g., 30s) and emit metric for cooldown-caused-blocks.

morgan: I'll trigger the forced refill now and monitor metrics. eva, please coordinate with CS to tell customer we did a forced refill and we're patching the refill retry path.

sre-bot: action triggered: admin.refill_pool(tenant=5f8a9c, pool=eu-west-3-gpud-1) by morgan at 2678912360 :white_check_mark:

morgan: Refill RPC succeeded on attempt 2 after we retried from control-plane console. Credits jumped from 0 -> 1200 in the metric feed. 429s stopped ~20s after refill.

eva: Customer confirmed recovery and provided their retry timestamps. They had heavy client-side aggressive retries which amplified pressure. Suggested mitigation to them: smoother exponential backoff + client-side jitter.

ira: I'll open an infra ticket for: - refill RPC retry/backoff - cooldown cap - telemetry for cooldown blocks + automated alert when refill failures > 2. Assign to eng-infra.

alex-p: Also add a short KB note for CS: "If credits don't refill after throttle removal" with the manual refill admin step and typical root causes (RPC failure, node pressure, aggressive client retries).

morgan: Thanks team. Logging followup notes into the incident tracker. :thumbsup:
